h: Tips for a good market morning
p: Get there early if you can. The best of the bread, pies and cakes can sell out by late morning, and the earlier you arrive, the more choice you'll have and the more chance there is to chat to the stallholders before it gets busy.

Bring a cool bag if you're planning to pick up meat, cheese or anything else that needs keeping chilled, especially in warmer weather. A couple of reusable bags will save juggling armfuls of veg back to the car, and it's handy to have a bit of change for smaller stalls, even though many take cards these days.

Don't be afraid to ask questions. Farmers market traders are usually happy to tell you how something was grown or made, suggest a recipe or point you to a seasonal favourite. You might come home with a new favourite sausage or chutney you'd never have found in the supermarket.

The windmill itself is worth a proper look while you're there. Marsh Mill has been part of the Thornton skyline for well over two centuries, a handsome reminder of the area's farming past when the flat Fylde fields were dotted with mills grinding local grain. It makes a lovely backdrop for a photo with your shopping.

Once you're done, there are some lovely spots nearby to make a morning of it. Wyre Estuary Country Park is just a short hop away, with walks along the river and plenty of birdlife. Or head to Cleveleys promenade, where sculptures along the seafront tell a playful story drawn from local myths and legends, before tucking into fish and chips.
